summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator and Tresting survey a ruined office after an attack in which four Korean gang members, all teenagers, lie dead. Tresting, a black private investigator, thanks the narrator for saving his life, and the two wonder whether the attack was carried out by Pithica, an apparent adversary. The narrator is shaken by the children's deaths and the realization that Pithica may be behind the violence and wants it left uninvestigated.
one_line: After an attack leaves four teenage gang members dead in a ruined office, Tresting and the narrator suspect Pithica is behind it.
key_facts: The narrator knows they sustained five shallow cuts on their face, neck, and hands, and considers none of them worth worrying about.
Four dead teenagers, a girl and three boys, are described as probably around fifteen or sixteen years old.
The narrator says, "I hate it when bad things happen to kids. Especially when I'm the bad thing."
Tresting says the dead are Korean and gang members, pointing to a blood-smeared tattoo on one boy's hand.
The narrator recalls something about race riots and makes a mental note to ask the Internet about it.
Tresting looks out through the shattered window and then at the narrator with disbelief, and the narrator feels smug.
Tresting checks the girl's wrist for a pulse that the narrator knows will not be there.
Tresting says, "They would've killed me," and adds, "This neighborhood, cops would've been too slow."
Tresting says it is the first time Pithica has targeted him.
Tresting recites that a black PI attacked by Korean gang members in a bad neighborhood would be written off by cops as a hate crime.
Tresting reminds the narrator, "You saw the data, Russell. Hell, you've been attacked."
Tresting concludes that Pithica does not want the attack investigated, and says, "They're killing people".
